description: Configure the web server or reverse proxy to enforce the SameSite attribute (Lax or Strict) on all Set-Cookie response headers. When SameSite=Lax is set, browsers do not include the cookie in cross-site POST, PUT, DELETE, or other state-changing requests initiated from a different origin. When SameSite=Strict is set, cookies are not included in any cross-site navigation. This prevents CSRF attacks because the attacker cross-origin request arrives without the victim session cookie, making it unauthenticated. Modern browsers default to SameSite=Lax for cookies that omit SameSite, but applications that explicitly set SameSite=None (for cross-origin API use) or legacy applications that predate the default bypass this protection. Admin enforcement at the proxy layer overrides the application cookie attributes.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: The attacker must find a way to bypass the SameSite restriction (e.g., exploit a subdomain XSS vulnerability to achieve same-site context, or target a browser that does not enforce SameSite) to include the victim session cookie in a cross-site request. Without this bypass, cross-site state-changing requests arrive unauthenticated and are rejected by the application.

verification.method: Verify that all Set-Cookie response headers include SameSite=Lax or SameSite=Strict. Check web server or reverse proxy configuration for cookie attribute enforcement directives.

commands.expected: Non-empty output — Apache mod_headers SameSite enforcement directive found
Non-empty output — nginx SameSite cookie flag directive found
SameSite=Lax or SameSite=Strict on all Set-Cookie headers

remediation.name: Apache mod_headers SameSite=Lax enforcement on all cookies

steps.description: Create an Apache drop-in config that rewrites all Set-Cookie headers to include SameSite=Lax. The Header edit directive appends SameSite=Lax to cookies that do not already carry a SameSite attribute, and rewrites SameSite=None to SameSite=Lax for cookies that explicitly disabled it.
steps.command:
printf '<IfModule mod_headers.c>
  Header always edit Set-Cookie "(?i)^((?!.*SameSite).*)$" "$1; SameSite=Lax"
  Header always edit Set-Cookie "(?i)(SameSite=None)" "SameSite=Lax"
</IfModule>
' > /etc/httpd/conf.d/cme-916-samesite.conf

steps.description: Test the Apache configuration for syntax errors before reloading
Gracefully reload Apache to apply the new cookie header rules

remediation.name: nginx proxy_cookie_flags SameSite=Lax enforcement on all proxied cookies

steps.description: Create an nginx drop-in config snippet that adds the SameSite=Lax flag to all cookies set by upstream backends via proxy_cookie_flags. Requires nginx 1.19.3+ (included in RHEL 9+, Fedora, Ubuntu 22.04+).
Test the nginx configuration for syntax errors before reloading
Gracefully reload nginx to apply the new cookie flag rules
